Core Active Vocabulary (8 items):

apple — a round red or green fruit. Example: There are some apples in the fridge.
banana — a long yellow fruit. Example: I have got two bananas.
orange — a round orange fruit. Example: I have got an orange.
potato — a round vegetable that grows in the ground. Example: We need a kilo of potatoes.
meat — the flesh of animals used as food. Example: There isn't any meat in the fridge.
chicken — a bird used as food. Example: I would like the chicken, please.
milk — a white drink from cows. Example: There is some milk in the fridge.
cheese — a food made from milk. Example: There is some cheese on the plate.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• There are some ...
• There is some ...
• We haven't got any ...
• It is a fruit.
• It is a vegetable.

Grammar focus: Countable & Uncountable Nouns + Quantifiers.
Countable foods have plurals: an apple, two apples. Uncountable foods have no plural: milk, cheese, meat. Use some with both, and any in questions and negatives.
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.
Choose the correct sentence.
Choose the uncountable food.

Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
In my fridge there are some apples and two bananas. There is some milk and some cheese, but there isn't any meat. I have got an orange and a potato.
